content.title: About
content.content: Grapefruit (Citrus × paradisi) is a large, round citrus fruit with a yellow to pinkish skin and juicy white, pink, or red flesh. It has a tangy, slightly bitter flavor. The fruit is a hybrid of pomelo and sweet orange that originated in Barbados. Grapefruit is eaten fresh and juiced, and used in salads and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Grapefruit is a hybrid of pomelo and sweet orange.
It is named for the way the fruit grows in clusters on the tree, like grapes.
Pink and red grapefruit get their color from lycopene, the same pigment in tomatoes.
The bitterness comes from compounds such as naringin, found mainly in the white pith and membranes.
Grapefruit can strongly interact with many medications.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Grapefruit provides vitamin C, which supports the immune system and skin.

items.title: Contains lycopene and vitamin A
items.content: Pink and red grapefruit provide lycopene and carotenoids with antioxidant properties.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Eating the whole fruit adds fiber that supports digestion.

items.title: Hydrating and low in calories
items.content: Grapefruit is juicy and relatively low in calories.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice can interfere with how the body processes many medications, including some statins, blood pressure drugs, and immune-suppressing drugs, and can raise their levels in the blood. If you take prescription medication, ask a doctor or pharmacist before eating grapefruit.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acid in grapefruit may trigger heartburn or reflux in sensitive people and may wear down tooth enamel.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some people may be allergic to grapefruit or other citrus fruits.

items.title: Potassium considerations
items.content: People with kidney problems should ask a healthcare professional about potassium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Grapefruit can be halved and eaten with a spoon, peeled and eaten in segments, added to salads, juiced, or broiled with a little honey. Cutting away the white pith and membranes reduces bitterness. Always check with a healthcare professional first if you take prescription medication.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Grapefruit can be kept at room temperature for about a week or refrigerated for two to three weeks. Cut grapefruit should be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator and eaten within a couple of days. Fresh juice should be refrigerated and drunk within a day or two.
